judgment.summary: The coupled conversation path is satisfactory in the exercised scope: attachment disclosure, manual reading position, return to latest, Stop focus and failure/retry worked.
judgment.scope: Initial blind product judgment, not final release acceptance.

findings.observation: The source-family sidebar, centered reading column and composer remain coherent in original light/dark desktop, narrow reading and compact six-line captures. File-family source is byte-identical to the foundation.
Keyboard filename disclosure and Escape restored the trigger; removing a file restored composer focus. The filename-only synthetic adapter matched the foundation.
Manual scrollTop stayed 0 while content height grew 1277 to 1625 px. Return to latest had bottom gap 0 at all three samples across approximately 1.5 seconds of continued streaming.

Keyboard Stop restored composer focus by the first 100 ms sample. After settling, body text length stayed stable over 500 ms. Forced failure/retry completed Observation theme 7, and reload returned to the seeded state.

Horizontal attachment browsing preserves height but leaves some files outside the visible strip. Full-name modal disclosure blurs the reading context; the viewed narrow filename breaks working between lines.
Full assistive-technology behavior, arbitrary attachment counts, extreme composer growth, all edit/branch actions and physical touch behavior were not certified.

judgment.summary: Core settings behavior and representative long-value presentation are supported. The expanded narrow navigation pushes primary editing down and remains a hierarchy caveat.
judgment.scope: Initial blind product judgment; narrow polish is qualified, and final release acceptance is not implied.

findings.observation: Tabler-native labels, helper text, state wording and tinted error/status feedback form a coherent settings surface in both themes.
At 390 px, display name and organization wrapped the representative long bilingual value in textareas with clientWidth=scrollWidth=330 and clientHeight=scrollHeight=78.
The full vertical settings navigation precedes the form. The display-name field begins around y=765 and organization around y=910.5 in the 390×844 view, making primary editing less prominent.

The authoritative store and distribution assets matched the foundation. Submitted snapshot saving preserved later draft edits; Cancel, failure preservation, current-draft retry, invalid-name focus and short-name reload persistence succeeded.
Native disabling briefly moved pending Save focus to BODY. Completion restored Save when focus was abandoned and did not steal it from continued editing.
The run did not exhaust all validation/toggle permutations, storage corruption/quota behavior, extreme unbroken input strings or assistive-technology paths.

material_unresolved_items: Narrow settings navigation hierarchy remains a polish caveat; no failed persistence path was observed.

judgment.summary: The settled native Tabler action-toast integration is satisfactory in the exercised bounded scope, including failed-snapshot retry and focus recovery.
judgment.scope: Initial blind judgment against the settled T4 integration; inherited broader settings issues are outside its redesign scope.

findings.observation: The source toast header/body/separated action row, standard width, typography, border, shadow and native close remain recognizable in the assembled product. Source preview, store, dist and preview assets matched the foundation.

A valid submitted snapshot saved while later edits stayed in the form. Failure preserved prior storage. Retry saved the failed snapshot while preserving a newer draft and an accurate unsaved-edit summary.

Pending Save remained focused using a disabled visual class and aria-disabled plus a guarded handler. Focus returned to Save when Retry disappeared and when the toast closed; invalid-name submission focused the associated field.
Success wording and time followed authoritative store events. Toast role=status, polite live region and aria-atomic coexist with an aria-live=off inline summary.

Prescribed fixed top-right placement remains contained at narrow width but can overlay header or upper form content. Long navigation and single-line identity clipping are inherited broader settings limitations.
All possible dismissal/result races, concurrent operation orderings, gallery menus and screen-reader announcement behavior were not exercised.

judgment.summary: The expressive paper/serif research workspace and native edit/save/disk/reload path are supported. Narrow tables require local panning, and reduced motion retains a shortened transition.
judgment.scope: Initial blind product judgment; table access and motion limits remain explicit, with no general accessibility or motion-comfort certification.

findings.observation: A populated paper-like sheet, warm light/dark surfaces, serif English text, red margin, separate right navigation and ruled native editor establish a distinct whole-workspace treatment. Bundled source identifies Vanilla Paper 0.10.0 by Simon Huber with MIT license; the supplied TiddlyWiki vendor files matched the foundation.
Native search/related-note navigation, bilingual passage edits, save, exact disk text, reload agreement, cancelled-draft preservation and continuing to the unfinished note succeeded.
Native Vanilla Paper Day/Night palette selections and Simplified Chinese UI selection succeeded; long bilingual content was inspected in the declared viewport/theme conditions.

The approximately 483 px ledger table is inside a 318 px local overflow-x:auto region. Actual horizontal wheel input reached the rightmost Does not establish column without widening the 390 px document. Initial offscreen columns have limited explicit disclosure.

The page-container transition changes from 0.4 s normally to 0.15 s under reduced motion. A real keyboard sidebar toggle still had intermediate positions. A later universal 150 ms rule overrides the earlier 1 ms rule, so the behavior is shortened rather than instant.

Keyboard/touch access to all table columns, server-outage recovery, every native wiki tool, assistive-technology access, upstream acquisition authentication, resource profiling and natural-speed motion comfort were not established.

material_unresolved_items: Table scrolling requires lateral panning and has limited disclosure; keyboard/touch panning was not certified.
Reduced motion retains a 150 ms sidebar/layout transition rather than eliminating motion.

judgment.summary: Reading, attachments, return to latest and failure/retry are supported, but keyboard Stop loses focus to BODY and requires a consequential detour back to the composer.
judgment.scope: Initial blind product judgment. Full T2 keyboard-continuity scope remains unresolved; no repair was made.

findings.observation: The mature workspace, compact File-family attachment strip, six-line composer and explicit text-bearing Return to latest control remain coherent across the viewed light/dark and narrow/compact conditions. File source and the synthetic adapter matched the foundation.

Full filename dialog disclosure, Escape trigger return and remove-to-composer focus worked. Manual scrollTop stayed 0 while height grew 1277 to 1599 px; return-to-latest bottom gaps stayed 0 across approximately 1.5 seconds while streaming.
The forced partial response failure was clearly visible; keyboard retry completed the long fixed response and reload returned to the seeded in-memory state.

Keyboard Stop ended the stream and text stabilized, but activeElement was BODY at 100 ms and remained BODY around 1.1 and 1.6 seconds. A separate targeted run reproduced the loss and required 12 Tabs through other controls to reach the composer.
After the 12-Tab recovery, a keyboard follow-up could be sent. This is a substantial continuity defect, not a complete keyboard trap or evidence of indefinite post-stop generation.
The horizontally browsed attachment strip hides some files outside the current view, and modal filename disclosure temporarily obscures the reading context.
All editor/branch paths, arbitrary content extremes, physical touch behavior and assistive-technology behavior were not certified.

material_unresolved_items: Keyboard Stop focus restoration requires a separately retained authorized repair and verification before unqualified T2 acceptance.
